how.title: How it works
how.intro: Fight cards run long and nobody knows when the main event will start. FightWake watches the card so you don't have to.

steps.title: Pick a bout
steps.body: Open any upcoming fight card and tap the fight you want to see.

steps.title: Choose when
steps.body: Get woken when the bout starts, when the fighters walk out, or one bout before.

steps.title: Go to sleep
steps.body: We follow the card live and wake you when it's time, whether the fights before yours end early or go the distance.

items.title: A real alarm
items.body: A full-screen alarm that rings through silent mode and Do Not Disturb, even on a locked phone.

items.title: No spoilers
items.body: You never see a result. Watch the fight live or catch the replay without knowing who won.

items.title: Backup alarm
items.body: If your phone loses signal overnight, a backup alarm still rings at the estimated time.

items.title: Follows the card live
items.body: Quick finishes, decisions and canceled bouts all move your alarm. If your fight is canceled, we tell you.

items.title: Free notifications
items.body: Get a notification when any bout starts, main event included, on every card.

items.title: Five languages
items.body: English, Spanish, French, Russian and Hebrew. Fighter names stay as you know them.

items.q: What time does the UFC main event start?
items.a: Nobody can say exactly. The main event starts when every fight before it is over, so a night of quick finishes can bring it forward by an hour and a night of decisions can push it back. FightWake follows the card live and wakes you based on what actually happens.

items.q: How do I wake up for a UFC fight without seeing the results?
items.a: Set an alarm for the bout in FightWake. The app only tracks which fight is on, never who won, so you can wake up and watch without spoilers.

items.q: Will the alarm ring if my phone is on silent?
items.a: Pro alarms ring through silent mode and Do Not Disturb. Free notifications follow your phone's sound settings and can arrive a little late while the phone is asleep.

items.q: What if the fight before mine ends early?
items.a: Your alarm moves with the card. If you chose one bout before, it rings as soon as that bout ends, whether it lasted 30 seconds or went to the scorecards.
